title: Efficient Synthesis of Multi-Controlled Toffoli Gates with Ternary Clifford$+P_9$ Gates
abstract: Temporary occupation of qutrit levels can reduce the width and depth required for binary circuit logic in quantum computing. We introduce an efficient intermediate-qutrit decomposition of multi-controlled Toffoli gates with binary-subspace inputs and outputs. For balanced control widths $n=2^h-1$, the proposed decomposition is evaluated hierarchically through a tree, allowing independent subtree computations to proceed in parallel and reducing the depth from linear to logarithmic. The balanced low-depth construction requires $6n+3$ logical $P_9$ injections and $\frac{n-3}{4}$ clean ancillary qutrits. It matches the direct $P_9$ count of a recursively extended Clifford+$P_9$ baseline derived from the state-of-the-art work while using asymptotically one-quarter as many clean ancillas and replacing linear depth with logarithmic depth. For arbitrary control widths, a sequential extension preserves the $6n+3$ $P_9$ count but has depth $O(\log m+n-m)$ for a balanced core $m=2^h-1\leq n$, which is linear in the worst case over $n$. By reducing the resource overhead of a widely used reversible primitive, the proposed decomposition provides a practical building block for the design and compilation of more resource-efficient quantum algorithms in the fault-tolerant regime.
summary: This paper presents an efficient method to synthesize Multi-Controlled Toffoli gates using a ternary qutrit system. By employing a hierarchical, tree-based decomposition, it reduces the circuit depth from linear to logarithmic scaling for balanced control widths. This offers a practical, resource-efficient building block for advanced fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently synthesizing Multi-Controlled Toffoli (MCT) gates, which are crucial primitives for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: A novel intermediate-qutrit decomposition achieves logarithmic depth scaling ($\Theta(\log n)$) for balanced control widths, significantly outperforming linear-depth recursive baselines.
method: The authors propose a hierarchical, tree-based decomposition strategy utilizing temporary occupation of a third qutrit level to evaluate multi-controlled logic.
model_or_system: The work is set in a ternary qutrit model ($\mathcal{H}_3$) where the computation logic is confined to a binary subspace, using the third level as a temporary workspace state.
key_observables: Logical P9 injection count ($6n+3$), clean ancillary qutrit count ($n-3/4$), and circuit depth ($\Theta(\log n)$).
important_parameters: Control width ($n$), balanced core width ($m=2^h-1$), and the underlying resource model (ternary Clifford+P9).
main_assumptions: The decomposition relies on the temporary occupation of the qutrit level $|2angle$, and comparisons are made within the specific ternary Clifford+P9 resource model.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the overall decomposition structure, detailing the forward tree computation (leaf blocks, internal merges, root toggle) and the inverse traversal for state restoration.
paper_structure: The paper develops the tree computation via leaf and internal merge blocks, analyzes the resource costs for balanced widths ($n=2h-1$), and then extends the construction to arbitrary widths by appending sequential controls, comparing results against established recursive baselines.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation, the resource optimization techniques (depth reduction, ancillary qubit minimization) are highly relevant to designing efficient quantum circuits for physical platforms like trapped ions or superconducting qubits where gate depth and ancillary overhead are primary limitations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Balanced qubit-qutrit predicate tree. Each leaf block Lj uses a ternary Clifford SUM gate and one state-selective C2(INC) operation to generate a temporary subtree marker. Each internal merge Mj uses one branch-local clean ancillary qutrit and three state-selective increments to combine two child markers with the corresponding middle control. After the complete all-controls-satisfied predicate reaches the root, the unique strict toggle C2(X01) acts on the target. The inverse tree restores all temporary marker states and returns every ancillary qutrit to |0⟩.

FIG. 2. Decomposition of a seven-controlled MCT gate. The logical controls are q0, . . . , q6 and the target is q7. Red circles denote activation on |1⟩, whereas blue circles denote activa- tion on |2⟩. The ternary Clifford SUM and SUM† gates gener- ate and uncompute the two leaf markers. The state-selective C2(INC)±1 operations propagate and remove the complete all-controls-satisfied predicate using the clean ancillary qutrit a. The root marker activates the unique strict target toggle C2(X01). The circuit requires 45P9 injections and one clean ancillary qutrit.
